BLOCKER: 0014 creates `audit_id_seq` with no USAGE grant to pf_app/pf_runtime, and `Swap`/`Down` only grant INSERT/SELECT on the table; `DEFAULT nextval(...)` is privilege-checked against the inserting role, so the first app audit write after the swap fails 42501. Append's heal only matches 23514, so the audit write path hard-fails post-swap.

Integration tests insert as the pool/owner role (and pre-swap into the flat table), so the missing post-swap sequence grant is untested; the AC's "freshness/monotonicity after swap as the app role" proof is absent.
MAJOR: `backup()` deadlocks on any early `obj.Put` failure (SSE/config/size): nothing drains the `io.Pipe`, `age` blocks writing, and `dump.Wait()` hangs the swap tool with no context timeout on the dump pipeline.

`PlaceHold` — the only code emitting `audit_hold_after_purge_total` — is not wired to any pfaudit-retention subcommand; holds can only be placed via raw SQL as pf_owner, so the spoliation metric/alert can never fire in production.

edpsvc reimplements coverage/staleness logic (`coverageStatus`, `rotationMaxAge`, `readCoverage`) and a parallel metrics JSON instead of reusing `pfaudit.CheckCoverage`/`EmitCoverage`; the added `replace productforge/pfaudit` is unused — two drifting implementations of one operational contract.

0014's seed block runs `min(at)`/`max(id)` over the entire legacy `audit` table inside the migration transaction; on a large production log this is a long-running migration holding transactional locks — needs a bounded pre-check or documented estimate step.

`edpdata.Append`'s comment ("the audit_provision trigger attaches a missing month") and `DROP FUNCTION audit_provision()` in the down migration reference a fast path 0014 never creates (section 10 is empty) — shipped code and SQL disagree about the insert path.
`VerifyHoldExtractionFrom` builds per-month digests with unbounded `string_agg` over the whole month (twice), O(month) DB memory — contradicts the scalability intent when export already streams.
MINOR: RLS test proves cross-tenant isolation only on the parent; "cannot read another tenant's rows through any path" is not asserted for direct leaf SELECTs (only leaf INSERT denial is tested).
Fresh-install AC case (empty audit → setval to 1) is neither implemented (`GREATEST(max, last_value)+1` yields 2 on a fresh sequence) nor tested.
Backup rehearsal asserts `SEQUENCE public audit_legacy_id_seq` but not `audit_id_seq`; S1 requires the sequence present.
s3store unknown-size (streamed) Put returns empty `Checksum` and `Version`; any caller relying on `Version` for versioned Get silently loses it for backups.
Plaintext NDJSON evidence is staged in `os.TempDir` before upload; allow a configurable/encrypted staging dir for legal evidence.
`architect_review.py`/config changes (retry/backoff, EXCLUDE glob rewrites, token/timeout, 180KB diff cap) are unrelated scope creep on an audit-partitioning item.
NIT: `audit_partition_config` as BOOLEAN PK with `CHECK (id)` is an odd singleton idiom; a constant-key table reads clearer.
`CoverageStatus.LastRotationAgeHours < 0` sentinel plus a separate `Stale` bool is redundant with the emitted gauge.
Down migration drops `audit_provision()`, a function 0014-up never creates.
SUMMARY: Strong overall design: catalog-driven resumable swap, fail-closed retention/holds, privilege-enforced hardening and good crash-ordering (record-before-destroy) are all real and largely tested against PG16.
One blocker must be fixed before merge: no USAGE grant on the new `audit_id_seq` breaks every app audit insert the moment the swap commits, and no test exercises the app-role write path post-swap.

Top risks after that: the pg_dump/age pipe deadlock in `backup`, no shipped operator path for placing legal holds (metric dead), and duplicated coverage logic between edpsvc and pfaudit that will drift.
